results.quantity: Matched-beam CH3OH comparison at the Band-5 peak pixel (all data convolved to 9.36x6.28" PA -88): extended vs compact, and excitation
results.value: Q J=1-3: 1.71+-0.06 K km/s; 2(0)-1(-1) E: Xb4f 0.263+-0.028, Xb4d 0.146+-0.016 K km/s (Xb4d recovers only 55+-8% of the Xb4f flux: CH3OH is extended/resolved out at 0.9"); 5(-2,4)-4(-1,3) E (Eu 57 K): 0.035+-0.032 (Xb4f), 0.018+-0.015 (Xb4d), J=4..8 Q-branch <0.3. LTE (A, Trot) fit: Trot=9 K (1 sigma 8-9, 3 sigma 7-10 K) but chi2=53 for 6 dof: LTE is not a good description (Q J=1-3 under-predicted by 1.6x). RADEX (LAMDA e-ch3oh, n 1e2-1e8, Tkin 10-200 K, eta free) also fails (chi2min 55 for 5 dof; best Tkin=10 K, n>=1e7, N/eta degenerate). Conclusion: CH3OH rotational excitation is LOW (Trot<~15 K; Eu>45 K lines absent) or non-LTE; no useful density/column constraint; beam-averaged N_u(2_0, Eu=20 K)=1.7e12 cm-2 over 9.4x6.3" (N(E-CH3OH) of order 1e13-1e14 cm-2 for Trot~10 K, uncertain by >1 dex). Q-branch/2(0)-1(-1) ratio is the discriminator

results.value: Template = HCN 4-3 profile of the region; CO wing fitted simultaneously (exponential, log-quadratic, log-cubic, power-law, Lorentzian; range 341.80-342.20 GHz; models with chi2/dof>1.3 rejected: Lorentzian, and the zero-CO case is excluded by chi2=695-1456 for 102 points). Accepted models: 3-sigma upper limit H13CN/HCN(4-3) < 0.09-0.11 (N), < 0.135-0.15 (S; log-quadratic/cubic only), < 0.075-0.15 (Bridge) i.e. HCN/H13CN > 9 (N), > 6.7 (S, Bridge); N best-fit alpha=0.015-0.045+-0.015 (<=3 sigma). Earlier zero-CO limits (0.15/0.45/0.24 from the half-profile) were looser but unmodelled. The limit is conditional on the wing family; with a free CO wing a real H13CN signal of this size is degenerate with the wing, so the limit is the minimum defensible; extending the fit to 342.28 GHz (CO core) gives similar numbers only for log-quadratic/cubic models

results.quantity: Cross-check with the literature (Harada+2018 ApJ 855, 49, ALMA Band 3 line survey of NGC 3256; Sato+2022 A&A, APEX/NOEMA)
results.value: Agreements: CH3OH, SO, HOC+ and HCN/HCO+ detected there too; Harada+ report the largest chemical variation in CH3OH (and SiO), and CH3OH emission at the two nuclei "not dominant", more visible in tidal arms/outflow positions - consistent with our CH3OH peaking on the Bridge and W clump and being undetected at the N and S nuclei (<1.7% of HCO+) in Xb4d. HOC+ remains tentative here (3 sigma conservative) whereas Harada+ detect it at the central position (low-excitation lines). Not checked: SiO (not covered), H2CS (blended with CS 7-6 here, limit <0.34). Cross-check made from the published abstracts/summary only (tables not reproduced); status: partial

results.quantity: Q1: Matched-beam statement for every Q1 ratio
results.value: Same-J HCN/HCO+ pairs: same OUS, same pixel grid, both cubes convolved to the same circular beam (1.05", 6.5" or 10") with the image-plane kernel of scripts/matched.py, moment-0 over +-350 km/s, brightness temperature conversion for the common beam; cross-band ladder ratios: 10" (2-1/3-2/4-3) or 6.5" (3-2/4-3). Replaces the unmatched peak-pixel ratio entry of p0001 (N 0.61/0.88/1.04 across Xb4f/Xb4d/Xb4b was a beam effect: matched values are 0.52 / 0.81 / 0.80)

interpretation: Line inventory (corrected): besides HCN and HCO+ (J=2-1,3-2,4-3) and CS 7-6, CH3OH is detected (Band 5 165 GHz Q-branch J=1-3 at 27 sigma; 2(0)-1(-1) E at 254.015 GHz at 10 sigma), SO 5(4)-4(3) (Band 5, 8 sigma) is detected, HOC+ is tentative; everything else is a limit, blended or an edge artefact. CH3OH is cold/subthermal (Q-branch J>=4 and Eu>45 K lines absent; LTE Trot~9 K, but LTE and RADEX fits are poor) and extended: the Xb4d (0.9") CH3OH flux is only ~55% of the 9"-beam value, and in Xb4d it peaks on the Bridge and a W clump, not on the N and S nuclei (CH3OH/HCO+ 0.05 there vs <0.015 at the nuclei) - a shock/low-excitation tracer signature that agrees qualitatively with Harada+2018. The extended disk is defined (Xb55 HCO+ 2-1 S/N>5 at r>8", HCN/HCO+(2-1)=0.51) but is not detected in the 3-2/4-3 data with the available sensitivity/zero-level. The southern blue-shifted component 1.9" south of S is statistically solid (7-12 sigma after null calibration, 0 null peaks above 8 sigma in 583 beams), has no red counterpart, is not a PSF-sidelobe copy of S, and has HCN/HCO+(3-2)~1.8 versus 0.4 at S; it is a separate broad component at ~2560-2650 km/s. The N and S nuclei are separable in Xb4b, Xb4d, Xb4f, Xb47 (not in Band 5). The opacity test (H13CN) can only give HCN/H13CN>7-9 (conditional on the CO-wing model). Raw HCN/HCO+ (3-2) peak ratios (N 0.6-1.0, S 0.4-0.5) are preliminary and not beam matched across OUS (Q1).
caveats: Peak-pixel intensities use different native beams per OUS; no cross-OUS ratio in this item is beam matched (Q1/Q6).

Systemic velocity 2780 km/s is a single adopted value; nuclear peak velocities differ by ~100 km/s at 0.25" (N 2811-2817, S 2710), so +-350 km/s windows are not centred on each nucleus; the HCN/HCO+ integrals use the same fixed window for both lines.

Line identifications rest on Splatalogue CDMS/JPL rest frequencies at v=2780 km/s; HOC+, SO 4_5-3_4 and both unidentified features need independent confirmation (e.g. matching J transitions at matched beam).
The Band-5 cubes do not separate N, S, Bridge (13% leakage at the nuclear separation, single HCO+ 2-1 peak pixel).
Empirical noise comes from emission-free pixels at 6-11" (primary-beam-corrected noise there is 1.2-1.6x the central value), which makes limits conservative by up to ~1.5x.
Xb4b nuclear emission is clumpy: peak-pixel values depend on the exact pixel chosen (search radius 1"); spectra are non-Gaussian (double-horned), Gaussian FWHM are indicative only.
No source of data for line-free-channel continuum from cubes exists (cubes are continuum-subtracted); the contamination check relies on mfs vs cont images, which have 1-2 sigma noise.
The 'aperture' (1.5" radius) rows of the line table use statistical noise only (no empirical null).
The conversion to K km/s uses the Rayleigh-Jeans formula with the beam of each cube; distance 40 Mpc is only used for pc sizes.

CH3OH LTE/RADEX fits have chi2/dof ~9-11: the numbers Trot=9 K and n>=1e7 are formal; the robust statement is 'Q-branch J>=4 absent: low excitation'. Baseline ripple of ~0.2 K km/s is visible in Band 5 (J=5 at -4 sigma).
Local-velocity matching (not 2780 km/s) is essential for identifications at S (2710-2740 km/s): at vsys the 251.66 feature would favour NS; at local velocity it clearly favours CH3OH.

The zero level of Xb4f/Xb55 moment-0 maps at r>8" is biased by about -0.5 / -1.3 Jy/b km/s (negative bowl, missing short spacings); disk fluxes are zero-level-corrected with the r=14-22" ring and carry >=0.3 Jy/b km/s systematic.

Soutflow position error is dominated by the assumed 10% beam pointing floor (0.10"), not by the fit (0.01-0.02"); wing definition relative to v_S=2722; comparison with the CO outflow geometry (Sakamoto+2014, Michiyama+2018) has not been made quantitatively.
H13CN limit conditional on the CO-wing family; log-quadratic/cubic wings can absorb a genuine H13CN signal.
Literature cross-check is from abstracts/summaries (Harada+2018, Sato+2022), not their tables.

Q1: ratio uncertainties are dominated by systematics (window truncation ~5%, absolute flux scale 10% per band); statistical errors are <=1% at the nuclei. Noise uses few line-free windows contaminated at times by weak lines (quietest quartile used), so faint-region limits are approximate.
Q1: regions use fixed nominal positions; the N ratio varies across its sub-clumps (IQR 0.05-0.09 at 1.05"), so a different aperture centre changes N by ~0.03-0.05.

Q1: the decline of HCN/HCO+ and the low 3-2/2-1, 4-3/3-2 ladder ratios at 10" mix Band 5, 6 and 7 data with different resolved-out fractions (Q6: Xb4f is the most complete Band 6 set); they should be treated as inputs to RADEX with 14% errors, not as evidence for a nuclear difference.

Q1: the Xb55 2-1 "disk" may include beam wings of the nuclei and NEclump; the ring zero level (-1.2 to -2.0 Jy/b km/s) is not present in line-free channels, so the sign of the correction is uncertain.
